title: event-fragmentation-reassembly-and-siem-windowing-notes-v0p1
content:
- parent_event_id: optional link to logical parent (for batched policy diffs)
- evidence_refs: array of stable object ids (comma-separated in metadata header) pointing to evidence-store artifacts
- sequence_hash: short deterministic fingerprint (SHA256 hex prefix) computed over the uncompressed payload for quick equality checks
- total_uncompressed_size: integer as string (bytes)
- watermark_ts: ISO-8601 used by reassembly to progress ordering and TTL decisions
- signature_kid: optional signing key id (for later verification)

Notes: all numeric/complex values are represented as strings in the audit envelope to avoid downstream typing issues in logging pipelines. The actual fragment body lives in an attachment blob that consumers can decompress using content_encoding + compression.

Reassembly algorithm (runtime semantics):
1) Ingest fragment -> parse header fields -> lookup or allocate reassembly buffer by event_id.
2) Verify fragment_index < fragment_count and sequence_hash consistency when multiple fragments share same index (defensive).
3) Append and persist fragment to the buffer storage (durable local or distributed cache) with metadata: first_received_at, last_updated_at, origin_shard.
4) Two triggers for finalization:
   - Count-based: when collected fragments == fragment_count -> assemble in fragment_index order, validate sequence_hash(es) against computed hash, mark final_event|export_ready.
   - Time-based: reassembly TTL (configurable default 6 minutes). If TTL elapses without all fragments, produce a partial export containing available pieces, evidence_refs, a partial_reassembly flag, and an explicit missing_fragments list.
5) When exporting to SIEM, emit a single logical event that carries: event_id, schema_version, final_flag (complete|partial), ordering watermark, compressed assembled payload, and a dedupe_key = sha256(event_id + sequence_hash).

Windowing, watermarks, and ordering: 
- Each reassembly buffer tracks watermark_ts which is max(created_at of fragments seen). We use the watermark to strictly order exports for the same logical stream (e.g., audit-indexed by resource id).
- To avoid head-of-line blocking: if fragment_count is large (>8) and fragments are slow, the system will split export into a primary index event (summary) and a follow-up evidence bundle export. Primary event contains metadata + first NKB of the payload to allow real-time alerting, follow-up evidence message links to full content.

SIEM export format and deduplication: 
- Export is a compact envelope: {event_id, schema_version, final_flag, summary, assembled_payload_gzip_base64, evidence_refs, dedupe_key, exported_at}.
- Deduplication key: dedupe_key ensures idempotent ingestion: SIEM should ignore identical dedupe_key within TTL window (48h by default).
- For partial exports we include missing_fragments array and reassembly_backoff_hint (seconds) so SIEM parsers can suppress false alerts and optionally poll evidence store.

Backcompat/versioning strategy (v1->v3):
- Fragment metadata must include schema_version. Receiver logic supports conversion table: v1->v2 shim, v2->v3 shim. Shims live in a single place (audit-shim service) to avoid ad-hoc conversions across multiple consumers.
- Dual-write: during migration we recommend dual-write physical fragments in both v2 and v3 envelopes when the payload reshape is non-trivial (e.g., moving from embedded evidence to evidence_refs). Dual-write should be guarded by a rollout flag and sampled at 10% initially.
- Contract stability: addition of new optional header fields is allowed; renaming or repurposing headers requires a major version bump and a deprecation window (90 days) with monitoring for dropped fragments.

Operational considerations and edge cases:
- Lost fragments: if fragment_count never resolves and TTL passes, mark the assembled event as partial and create a follow-up remediation ticket to fetch evidence by evidence_refs where possible.
- Out-of-order duplicates: dedupe using (fragment_id) + (sequence_hash). If duplicate fragment_index arrives with differing sequence_hash, treat as conflict: keep the fragment with latest signed created_at if signature_kid present, otherwise log conflict to forensics queue.
- Storage sizing: account for buffer retention = expected reassembly concurrency * average event size * safety factor 2. Default TTL 6m, peak QPS sizes must be load-tested.
- Metrics to track: fragment_ingest_rate, reassembly_complete_rate, partial_export_rate, average_reassembly_latency, conflict_rate, evidence_fetch_error_rate.

Migration playbook (high level):
1) Implement fragment metadata contract and reassembly library in a single service (audit-reassembly).
2) Create feature-flagged rollout for producers to emit fragment metadata version header.
3) Start dual-write for high-value flows (policy-snapshots, session-dumps) at 10% sample for 2 weeks, monitor conflict/partial rates.
4) Ramp to 100% and enable TTL-based partial export.
5) Turn on SIEM dedupe_key enforcement and retire legacy per-fragment exports.

Appendix: heuristics and sample knobs to tune per workload
- reassembly_ttl_seconds: 360 (default), 120 for real-time alerts flows
- max_fragments_warn: 8 -> trigger summary+followup pattern
- buffer_memory_soft_limit_bytes: 512MB per shard
- duplicate_conflict_policy: prefer_signed>latest_ts>first_seen

Open questions / items for review:
- Do SIEM partners accept a single compressed base64 assembled_payload, or do they require multipart attachments? (ask Infosec & Splunk/Elastic contacts)
- Should evidence_refs always be present even if evidence embedded? (tradeoff: cross-referencing vs single-file forensic snapshot)
- Mechanism for cryptographic provenance verification for reassembled events (signatures vs append-only ledger).

Next steps:
- Validate the proposed metadata set with product forensic use-cases (Rosa).
- Implement a lightweight reassembly test harness and run replay of 72h production traces in staging (Julian).
- Draft SIEM export sample payloads and reach out to 2 major partners to confirm dedupe semantics (Benji).
